newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's TMA to raise capital to 60 bln pounds.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's TMA to raise capital to 60 bln pounds.

text.p: Lebanese cargo carrier Trans Mediterranean Airlines (TMA) on Monday invited shareholders to subscribe to a new share issue to increase its capital to 60 billion Lebanese pounds.

TMA said in a statement published in Beirut newspapers a shareholders general assembly on Friday "decided to increase the company's capital in cash to 60 billion Lebanese pounds through the issue of 59,994,000 new shares of 1,000 pounds each."
TMA said subscriptions were open November 14 to December 14.

It said a new share of 1,000 pounds will be issued for every 10 existing 100-pound shares so that the company's current capital of six million pounds will be distributed over 6,000 new shares instead of 60,000 old shares.

TMA is owned by the Lebanese Company for Air Investment which is 73 percent owned by Farid Raphael, a prominent banker. Former education minister Najib Abu Haidar holds 10 percent, Druze leader Walid Jumblatt six percent and financier Georges Yaacoub five percent. The rest is owned by small investors.
On August 5, TMA suspended all air and land activities. Two of TMA's seven aircraft are currently on lease to Kuwait Airlines.
